html:
A Corsican-born French official who led the conquest of what the French called Mauritania from 1902 until he was killed at Tidjikja in May 1905.

A student of Islam, he worked through alliances with Sufi leaders, above all Shaykh Sidiyya of the Trarza region, and called his method peaceful penetration. He made Mauritania a separate French territory in 1904, ruled from Saint-Louis in Senegal. Followers of Shaykh Ma al-Aynayn, who led resistance from the north, killed him. Conquest of the Adrar took until 1909 and the far north until the 1930s. See French West Africa and Mauritania.
